tasks.title: Ports move to Common/Interfaces, the DbContext comes from a factory, and the unit of work is named
acceptance: MASTER-048 (the move): `src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Interfaces/` exists and contains exactly four files -- `IDungeonReadRepository.cs`, `IDungeonWriteRepository.cs`, `IUnitOfWork.cs`, `IUnitOfWorkFactory.cs`. `ls src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/IDungeon*.cs` fails with 'No such file or directory'. Every one of the four declares `namespace DungeonMaster.Application.Common.Interfaces;` -- `grep -c 'namespace DungeonMaster.Application.Common.Interfaces;' src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Interfaces/*.cs` returns 1 for each file. Moving the file while leaving the namespace as `DungeonMaster.Application.Features.Dungeons` is a blocking finding: contracts/coding-standards.md section 7 requires the folder to mirror the namespace, and CORE-029 plus XCUT-006 are both about the port having an address.

MASTER-048 (the ripple, and its exact size): `grep -rl '^using DungeonMaster.Application.Features.Dungeons;' --include=*.cs src/ | wc -l` returns **39** on the parent commit and **0** after this task -- the 39 is measured with that command run in the worktree, not estimated. The report quotes both numbers. Any file among the 39 that this task did not need to touch is named in the report with the reason.

MASTER-023 (the registration): `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` calls `services.AddDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>(...)` and NOT `services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(...)`. `grep -c 'AddScoped' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns **0**; it returns **2** on the parent commit, at lines 33 and 34. `IUnitOfWorkFactory` and `IDungeonReadRepository` are registered `AddSingleton`. `IDungeonWriteRepository` is NOT registered at all -- `grep -c 'IDungeonWriteRepository' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns 0 -- because `UnitOfWork` constructs it; a container registration for it re-opens the hole this task closes and is a blocking finding.

MASTER-023 (the scoped registration that is NOT a defect): `AddDbContextFactory` also registers `AppDbContext` itself as a scoped service -- the EF Core 10 API remarks for `EntityFrameworkServiceCollectionExtensions.AddDbContextFactory` state it verbatim, and we do not control that descriptor. The report states this so no reviewer reads it as a miss. What must be true instead is that nothing in `src/` ever resolves it: `grep -rn 'GetRequiredService<AppDbContext>\|GetService<AppDbContext>' --include=*.cs src/` returns nothing after this task and returns exactly one hit on the parent commit, at `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:48`.

MASTER-023 (no scope is opened in production any more): `grep -rn 'CreateScope\|CreateAsyncScope' --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure src/DungeonMaster.App src/DungeonMaster.Application` returns nothing after this task. It returns exactly one hit on the parent commit, `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:47`, inside `MigrateDatabase`. The 10 hits inside `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/` are the test suite building its own containers -- 6 in `ApplicationServiceRegistrationTests.cs` and 4 in `CommandValidatorCoverageTests.cs`, measured with the same command -- and they must all still be there afterwards.

MASTER-023 (the lifetime is observable, not just declared): a new test in `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/UnitOfWorkTests.cs` proves two contexts are distinct across two units of work and identical within one -- `CreateAsync_CalledTwice_ProducesTwoIndependentChangeTrackers` loads the same dungeon in two units of work and asserts the two returned `Dungeon` instances are NOT reference-equal, and `Dungeons_WithinOneUnitOfWork_ReturnsATrackedAggregate` asserts that after `LoadAsync` the aggregate's `EntityState` is `Unchanged` rather than `Detached`. The first test is the one that would have failed under the process-lifetime context INFRA-018 describes; the report says which assertion carries which half.

MASTER-092 (the commit boundary exists and the repository no longer owns it): `grep -c 'SaveChangesAsync' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/DungeonWriteRepository.cs` returns **0**; it returns **3** on the parent commit, at lines 32, 45 and 63. `SaveChangesAsync` appears in exactly one production file afterwards -- `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/UnitOfWork.cs` -- inside `CommitAsync`. The port surface matches contracts/persistence-ports-and-unit-of-work.md section 3 exactly: `void Add(Dungeon)`, `void Update(Dungeon)`, `Task<bool> RemoveAsync(Guid, CancellationToken)`, `Task<Dungeon?> LoadAsync(Guid, CancellationToken)`.

MASTER-092 (a failed mutation commits nothing, and that is proved not assumed): in `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/DungeonMutationExtensionsTests.cs`, both `MutateAsync` overloads have a case asserting `await unitOfWork.DidNotReceive().CommitAsync(Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())` when the mutation returns a failure, and a case asserting the same when the dungeon is not found -- four assertions across the two overloads. Session 2 froze the two overloads as deliberately duplicated, so a test written against only one leaves the other's short-circuit unproven. The pre-existing `MutateAsync_WithFailingMutation_DoesNotSave` assertions against `UpdateAsync` are rewritten onto `CommitAsync`, not deleted, and the report names them.

MASTER-033: `grep -n 'AddAsync' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/DungeonWriteRepository.cs` returns nothing. The add path is `dbContext.Dungeons.Add(dungeon);` and `IDungeonWriteRepository.Add` returns `void`. `DungeonWriteRepositoryTests.AddAsync_PersistsDungeon` is renamed to match the new method name and still passes, going through a unit of work for its commit; the report names the old and new test names.

MASTER-004: `grep -n 'AsSplitQuery' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/DungeonWriteRepository.cs` returns exactly one hit, inside `LoadAsync`. Evidence must be behavioural as well as textual, because a grep cannot show the query actually split: the implementer runs the existing `DungeonWriteRepositoryTests` with EF command logging on and quotes the number of SELECT statements `LoadAsync` issues before and after -- expected to rise from 1 to 3 (dungeon, areas, objects), which the implementer confirms or corrects from the log rather than restating from this criterion. All four test files under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/` still pass.

MASTER-049: `grep -n 'AsSplitQuery' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/DungeonReadRepository.cs` returns exactly one hit, inside `GetDetailAsync` and NOT inside `GetSummariesAsync` -- the summary projection has no collection navigation to split and adding it there is a review finding. `DungeonReadRepositoryTests` still passes, including the assertions at lines 77-79 that a floor's areas materialise. If EF cannot apply `AsSplitQuery` to this projection shape, the implementer stops and reports it rather than silently dropping the call; the criterion is not satisfied by a call that is present and inert.

MASTER-011: `MigrateDatabase(this IServiceProvider)` is gone; `MigrateDatabaseAsync(this IServiceProvider services, CancellationToken ct)` returning `Task` exists in its place, obtains the context from `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>.CreateDbContextAsync(ct)`, and calls `await dbContext.Database.MigrateAsync(ct)`. `grep -rn 'Database.Migrate()' --include=*.cs src/` returns nothing. This closes both halves INFRA-019 raises -- the async EF API required by dotnet-guidelines.md section 2.1, and the cancellation token required by backend-conventions.md section 6.

MASTER-012: in `src/DungeonMaster.App/MauiProgram.cs`, the `Directory.CreateDirectory(dbFolder)` call at line 118 on the parent commit and the migration call at line 139 on the parent commit both sit inside one `try` block. The `catch` is typed with a `when` filter or names concrete exception types -- `grep -n 'catch' src/DungeonMaster.App/MauiProgram.cs` shows no bare `catch` and no unfiltered `catch (Exception)`, per the rule MASTER-005 established in Session 2 -- and its body writes the exception to `System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine` naming which startup step failed. `CreateMauiApp` returns normally afterwards, so the shell starts. The migration call is bracketed by a `CancellationTokenSource` with a finite timeout, which is what converts INFRA-019's named `__EFMigrationsLock` indefinite-wait hazard into a caught, logged failure.

MASTER-012 (the half deliberately not done, declared rather than discovered): UI-002 also asks that the migration move off the construction path so first paint does not wait on it. That needs a loading state and a user-visible error surface, which is view work this session does not do, so the migration is still awaited synchronously during `CreateMauiApp` via `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()`. The report states this explicitly, states that the call cannot deadlock because it runs before the MAUI application loop installs a `SynchronizationContext`, and flags the cold-start half for the backlog. A reviewer must not treat the retained block as an oversight, and the implementer must not invent an error UI to close it.

MASTER-029 (CLR types, this task's half): `grep -rn 'DateTimeOffset' --include=*.cs src/ | grep -v '/Migrations/'` returns **nothing** after this task. It returns **10 lines across 5 files** on the parent commit, enumerated in contracts/persistence-contract-and-timestamps.md section 3. `Entity.cs` declares `public DateTime CreatedAt`, `public DateTime LastModified` and `Touch()` assigning `DateTime.UtcNow`; `grep -rn 'DateTime.Now' --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Domain` returns nothing. Both DTOs and the three test literals change in the SAME commit as `Entity.cs` -- leaving the entity at `DateTime` while a DTO parameter is still `DateTimeOffset` puts a conversion inside an EF expression tree and must not exist even transiently.

MASTER-029 (the audit is wrong about the shape, and the report says so): the escalation and INFRA-003 both describe 'CreatedAt and LastModified on all four entity types'. They are declared exactly ONCE, on `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs` lines 16 and 21, which all four entity types inherit -- `grep -rn ': Entity$' --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Domain` returns exactly `Area.cs:8`, `Dungeon.cs:6`, `Floor.cs:8` and `PlacedObject.cs:8`. The report confirms the Domain edit was three lines in one file and not eight properties across four.

MASTER-103 (this task's share only): both timestamp properties in `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs` carry a `<remarks>` block naming `docs/persistence-contract.md` by path. That file does not exist yet -- T2 creates it -- and that is expected; this criterion covers the pointer, not the document. XCUT-007 asks for the persistence consequence to be recorded 'next to the entities rather than in the configurations', and `Entity.cs` is where the type decision is actually made.

No migration, and that is deliberate: `git diff --name-only` for this task contains NO path under `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Migrations/`. The model snapshot is knowingly out of step with the model between this task and T2, which owns `Migrations/**` and authors the session's single migration covering every model change both tasks make. contracts/persistence-ports-and-unit-of-work.md section 9 and contracts/persistence-contract-and-timestamps.md section 5 both state this. A reviewer must not raise the missing migration as a finding against this task.

Scope held: `git diff --name-only` for this task lists only paths inside this task's `owns` globs. In particular `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContext.cs`, `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContextFactory.cs`, everything under `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/`, and `src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/DungeonDetailViewModel.cs` are untouched -- the first three belong to T2 and the last to T3, and T3 may be running concurrently. Any of them appearing is a blocking finding.

Test wiring written once: the substituted `IUnitOfWorkFactory` / `IUnitOfWork` / `IDungeonWriteRepository` chain lives in ONE new helper file, `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/UnitOfWorkSubstitute.cs`, and the 17 test files that call `Substitute.For<IDungeonWriteRepository>()` on the parent commit use it. `grep -rl 'Substitute.For<IDungeonWriteRepository>' --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Tests | wc -l` returns 17 on the parent commit; after this task the three-line substitute chain appears in one file. Repeating it in 17 files is a blocking finding.

Test fixture not duplicated: the four files under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/` keep the `SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:")` fixture at `DungeonWriteRepositoryTests.cs:12-32` on the parent commit and add only the small `TestDbContextFactory` in contracts/persistence-ports-and-unit-of-work.md section 8.2. That type implements `CreateDbContext()` only, because `IDbContextFactory<TContext>.CreateDbContextAsync(CancellationToken)` is a virtual interface member with a default implementation. A second fixture pattern is a blocking finding per contracts/coding-standards.md section 8.

Formatting: every file this task created reports `with CRLF line terminators` under `file <path>`, and `grep -rEn '^ +[^ *]' <the changed .cs files>` produces no output (tabs only). Every new public member -- `IUnitOfWork`, `IUnitOfWorkFactory`, both their members, the three renamed write-port members, `MigrateDatabaseAsync` -- carries XML documentation in the two-tab form dotnet-format.md section 9 requires, and `RemoveAsync` carries a `<returns>` tag saying what `true` and `false` mean and stating that neither says anything about whether a commit happened.

No regression: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` completes with 0 warnings and 0 errors under `TreatWarningsAsErrors` for both App target frameworks, and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo` passes with 0 failures and a total at or above **434** -- the measured baseline on the session's base commit `9903f405dc919f782ba9048cae9623bcf1d79297`, produced by that exact command run in the worktree. The 292 cited by the audit-era documents is stale and must not be used. The report quotes the starting and ending totals and names every pre-existing test it rewrote.

tasks.title: Make the EF model fit SQLite: value comparer, sentinel, dead DbSets, design-time path, one migration, and the written contract
acceptance: MASTER-015 (the comparer): `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/AreaConfiguration.cs` supplies a `ValueComparer<IReadOnlyList<PathSegment>>` alongside the existing `HasConversion` pair at lines 59-74 on the parent commit, with `SequenceEqual` for equality, an aggregated per-element hash, and `ToList()` for the snapshot -- the three-lambda shape the cited EF value-comparers page's `List<int>` example uses. `PathSegment` is a `record` (`src/DungeonMaster.Domain/ValueObjects/PathSegment.cs:18`), so its compiler-generated structural equality and `GetHashCode` are what the comparer composes; the report confirms it did not hand-roll element equality.

MASTER-015 (the defect is shown to exist, then shown to be gone): a new test file `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests.cs` contains `CommitAsync_AfterLoadingAnUnmodifiedArea_WritesNothing`: it seeds a dungeon with one floor and one area with a non-empty outline, opens a unit of work, loads the aggregate, mutates nothing, and asserts `CommitAsync` returns **0**. The implementer runs this test against the parent commit and quotes the value observed there -- expected to be non-zero because the property access mode is `PreferFieldDuringConstruction` and `Area.Outline` returns `_outline.AsReadOnly()`, a fresh wrapper on every call, so snapshot and current value are never the same reference. The implementer confirms or corrects that expected number from the actual run; a test that passes both before and after has not exercised the defect and does not satisfy this criterion.

MASTER-015 (re-scoped against the current code, not the audit text): INFRA-004 says the spurious writes compound 'with the long-lived context described in INFRA-018'. After T1 there is no long-lived context, so the cost is now bounded to one save of one aggregate -- every tracked `Area` in the loaded dungeon has its `Outline` column rewritten on each commit, rather than growing across a session. Separately, Session 2 changed `UpdateAsync` to call `Update` rather than `Attach`, but under T1's lifetime the load and the commit share a context so that branch is not taken on any handler path. The report states the re-scoped cost in those terms and does not repeat the audit's compounding claim as if it were still true.

MASTER-075: `grep -n 'HasDefaultValue' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/PlacedObjectConfiguration.cs` returns nothing -- the store default is dropped, which is INFRA-008's preferred direction now that the backfill it existed for has been applied. `Scale` travels as ordinary data and `AppDbContextModelSnapshot.cs` no longer records it as `ValueGeneratedOnAdd()`; the report quotes the snapshot line before and after. A test asserts that a `PlacedObject` persisted and reloaded keeps the scale it was constructed with, for a value other than 1.0f, so the criterion is not satisfied by the mapping change alone. `HasSentinel(0f)` is the alternative INFRA-008 also names and is NOT what this task does; if the implementer believes dropping the default is unsafe it stops and escalates rather than substituting.

MASTER-032: `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContext.cs` declares `Dungeons` and no other `DbSet` -- `grep -c 'DbSet<' src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContext.cs` returns 1, down from 3 (lines 18, 23 and 28 on the parent commit). Nothing in the solution read `dbContext.Floors` or `dbContext.Areas`: `grep -rn '\.Floors\b\|\.Areas\b' --include=*.cs src/` returns hits only on navigation properties (`dungeon.Floors`, `floor.Areas`) and on the view models' own `Floors` collection, and the report shows that separation rather than asserting it. `OnModelCreating` is unchanged -- `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly` discovers the entity types independently of the `DbSet` declarations, and the four configurations still apply, proved by the whole Infrastructure test suite passing.

MASTER-050: `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContextFactory.cs` no longer hard-codes `"Data Source=dungeon-master.db"`. It resolves the path from `args` or an environment variable, defaulting to the same `{LocalApplicationData}/DungeonMaster/dungeon-master.db` that `src/DungeonMaster.App/MauiProgram.cs` builds at lines 115-121 on the parent commit, so design time and run time resolve to one file. The `args` parameter is used and its XML documentation no longer says 'Not used'. The report states the exact resolution order it implemented and how a developer overrides it.

MASTER-029 (migration half) and the session's single migration: exactly ONE new migration is added under `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Migrations/`, covering the timestamp value rewrite AND the `Scale` default drop. `AppDbContextModelSnapshot.cs` is regenerated and `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` reports no pending changes; the report quotes that command's output. The value rewrite is hand-written `migrationBuilder.Sql(...)` inside the generated `Up` -- the scaffolder emits schema operations, not data ones -- and it covers all EIGHT columns: `CreatedAt` and `LastModified` on each of `Dungeons`, `Floors`, `Areas` and `PlacedObjects`.

MASTER-029 (the stored format is established by observation, not assumed): before writing the SQL, the implementer creates a database on the parent commit's model, writes a row, and quotes the raw value of `SELECT CreatedAt FROM Dungeons LIMIT 1`; then applies the migration and quotes it again; then reads the row back through `AppDbContext` and asserts the `DateTime` round-trips to the same instant. contracts/persistence-contract-and-timestamps.md section 5.1 deliberately gives NO format string because that experiment has not been run, and a criterion or an implementation that assumes one is a blocking finding. `Down` reverses the rewrite, and the migration file's own XML documentation states why reconstructing the `+00:00` offset is lossless for this data set specifically -- every value originated from `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`.

MASTER-103: `docs/persistence-contract.md` exists and contains all five sections contracts/persistence-contract-and-timestamps.md section 6 enumerates -- the target, the cheap-and-expensive CLR type table with a citation per row, the store-default hazard generalised from INFRA-008 with `Scale` as the worked example, the rule for the next type choice, and a pointer naming `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs`. The two `<remarks>` blocks T1 added in `Entity.cs` name this file by path, so the pointer resolves in both directions; the report confirms it followed the link.

MASTER-093 (what is closed): `docs/persistence-contract.md` carries a 'Migration history' section recording that commit `7a4bb2d` squashed six migrations onto a baseline whose identifier `20260805014736` had never existed before that commit, and quoting its decision -- 'Existing local databases are not compatible and must be deleted; nothing shipped on the old history.' The stale comment at `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/PlacedObjectConfiguration.cs:36` on the parent commit is DELETED, not reworded, because MASTER-075 removes the default it describes; `grep -rn 'DB default backs existing rows' --include=*.cs src/` returns nothing.

MASTER-093 (what is NOT closed, declared rather than discovered): INFRA-020 also suggests adding `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` to CI and having startup refuse an unrecognised `__EFMigrationsHistory` with a clear message. **There is no `.github/workflows` directory in this repository** -- `ls -d .github/workflows` fails with 'No such file or directory' -- so the CI half has nothing to attach to, and no task in this session may create a pipeline to give it somewhere to land. The startup-refusal half is the same user-visible error surface MASTER-012 defers. Both are carried to the backlog and the report names them. A criterion depending on CI existing is itself a blocking finding.

PlacedObjectConfiguration formatting, bounded: this file is space-indented on the parent commit (INFRA-006, tracked as a separate entry NOT in this session). New and edited lines in it are written with TABS per contracts/coding-standards.md section 1; the surrounding space-indented lines are left alone. `git diff --stat` for that file shows a small edit. Reindenting the whole file is out of scope and is a review finding, not a bonus.

The four timestamp `Property` calls are untouched: `git diff -- src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/` shows no change to the eight `builder.Property(x => x.CreatedAt).IsRequired()` / `.LastModified` calls at `AreaConfiguration.cs:51-57`, `DungeonConfiguration.cs:43-49`, `FloorConfiguration.cs:50-56` and `PlacedObjectConfiguration.cs:38-42` on the parent commit. `IsRequired()` is type-agnostic and needs no edit for the `DateTime` change. `grep -rn 'HasConversion<DateTime>' src/` returns nothing -- that is INFRA-003's converter option, which E3 rejected, and implementing it is a blocking finding.

Scope held: `git diff --name-only` for this task lists only paths inside this task's `owns` globs. In particular `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/`, `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/Persistence/UnitOfWork.cs`, `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs`, `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs` and `src/DungeonMaster.App/` are untouched -- they are T1's, already landed, and re-editing them is a blocking finding.

Formatting: every file this task created reports `with CRLF line terminators` under `file <path>`. `.cs` files are tab-indented. `docs/persistence-contract.md` is prose and matches whatever the existing files under `C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\docs\` already do; the report says which convention that was and how it checked. The generated migration files keep the scaffolder's own style and are not reformatted -- the audit excludes EF-generated code from style review for exactly this reason.

No regression: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` completes with 0 warnings and 0 errors under `TreatWarningsAsErrors` for both App target frameworks, and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo` passes with 0 failures and a total at or above the count T1 left. The report quotes the count this task started from and the count it ended with, and confirms that dropping two `DbSet` properties and a store default broke no existing persistence test.

tasks.title: The detail page awaits its load and stops swallowing an unusable dungeon id
acceptance: MASTER-017 (the discarded task): `grep -n '_ = LoadDungeonCommand' src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/DungeonDetailViewModel.cs` returns nothing. On the parent commit it returns one hit inside `ApplyQueryAttributes`, which sits at lines 91-97 there. The started load is held in a field the page can await -- UI-005's own suggested direction -- so a failed load is observed rather than captured on a `Task` nobody holds. `IQueryAttributable` is KEPT; UI-005 states it is the trim-safe option the Shell navigation documentation recommends over `QueryProperty`, and replacing it is a blocking finding.

MASTER-017 (the silent branch): when `id` is absent from the query dictionary or does not parse as a `Guid`, `ApplyQueryAttributes` sets `ErrorMessage` to a message naming the failure rather than falling through and doing nothing. `_dungeonId` is not left at `Guid.Empty` with the page live -- UI-005's concrete complaint is that every subsequent save then targets a dungeon that does not exist. The report states what the view model does instead, and whether it blocks saves, clears them, or both.

MASTER-017 (automated evidence): `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/` gains tests following the `RepoPaths` source-scanning idiom the `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/` suite already uses (`src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/RepoPaths.cs`), because `DungeonMaster.Tests` targets `net10.0` and cannot reference the multi-targeted App project -- XCUT-002, tracked separately and NOT fixed here. At minimum: a test asserting `ApplyQueryAttributes` contains no discarded-task assignment, and a test asserting the unparsable-id branch assigns `ErrorMessage`. Both fail on the parent commit; the report quotes both failures. The implementer states plainly that this is source scanning rather than behavioural execution, and does not present it as more than it is.

MASTER-017 (observable outcome): the app is run on Windows and the detail page is navigated to twice -- once with a valid dungeon id, once with a deliberately malformed one. The report confirms that the valid case still loads and paints the dungeon, and that the malformed case shows the error label rather than an empty page that silently accepts edits. On the parent commit the malformed case produces a permanently empty page with no message; the report says so from having tried it, not from inference. This is a manual observation for the same reason MASTER-001's was in Session 2.

The existing failure-surfacing work is not disturbed: `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/ViewModels/FailureIsSurfacedTests.cs` passes unmodified, or, if `ApplyQueryAttributes`'s new shape requires a change to it, the report names the change and why. `ErrorMessage` is the channel Session 2 established at `src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/DungeonDetailViewModel.cs:70-71` on the parent commit and this task reuses it rather than adding a second one. `grep -c 'ErrorMessage' src/DungeonMaster.App/ViewModels/DungeonDetailViewModel.cs` rises; the report quotes the before and after values.

Scope held: `git diff --name-only` for this task lists exactly the paths in this task's `owns`. This task is INDEPENDENT of T1 and T2 and runs concurrently with T1. In particular `src/DungeonMaster.App/MauiProgram.cs` is T1's and must not appear, and no `.xaml` file appears at all -- the error label this reuses already exists in `DungeonDetailPage.xaml` from Session 2. If a XAML change turns out to be genuinely required, the implementer stops and escalates rather than editing a file outside its ownership set.
No `try`/`catch` is added around a dispatch, and `NotNullConverter.cs` is untouched -- its defect is MASTER-007, Session 5. The report notes the interaction if one arises.

Formatting: any new file reports `with CRLF line terminators` under `file <path>`; tabs only in `.cs`; XML documentation on any new public member, and the updated `<param>` block on `ApplyQueryAttributes` no longer claims the query 'Must contain an `id` key with a valid `Guid` string' if the method now tolerates one that does not.

No regression: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` completes with 0 warnings and 0 errors under `TreatWarningsAsErrors` for both App target frameworks, and `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo` passes with 0 failures and a total at or above **434** -- the measured baseline on the session's base commit `9903f405dc919f782ba9048cae9623bcf1d79297`. The 292 cited by the audit-era documents is stale. The report quotes both totals.
